I farm in Quzhou County in southern Hebei, so I will keep my land in the pattern I trust most: winter wheat followed by summer maize. That fits my weather, my soil, my equipment, and the way I manage labor. I am 40, I need a plan that is steady and not too complicated, so I will not spread myself across many crops this year. Wheat and maize are the safest choice for me because I know their field work, fertilizer timing, irrigation, and pest pressure well. I will use improved or hybrid seed because I want stable yield and better resistance, not because I want to try something fancy. For wheat, I will focus on base fertilizer, a topdressing at jointing, a few irrigations if water allows, and disease control only when needed. After wheat harvest, I will quickly plant summer maize, keep fertilizer simple, irrigate at key stages, and control weeds and borers with limited sprays. I will use rotary tillage because it is practical for me and matches my machinery and time. My main goal this year is stable grain output and lower risk, so I will manage carefully rather than chase the highest possible yield.
